Hi Dylan,

Thanks for sending over the updated DPA draft. Our legal and security teams spot-checked the retention and deletion language and had a couple of asks before we loop in procurement for countersignature. Two items in particular: 

1) "Data closure": can you clarify whether Redwood will actively delete customer data from backups (including cold snapshots) within the 30-day erasure window or whether you will mark it as inaccessible and retain copies for an additional archive period? Our auditors want explicit language.

2) Backup copies and restoration: we retain shorter RPOs in prod; however, for regulatory reasons some of our logs must be kept for 12 months. Will Redwood accept a carve-out that allows HelioMetrics to request a longer retention for a named log stream, with associated billing/SLAs?

I've attached our redlines to the DPA (PDF) and a short ops spreadsheet showing the log streams. Can you please confirm what evidence you can provide for deletion (manifest or tombstone entry, audit log entry, or certificate of destruction)?

Appreciate a quick call if that's easier.

Alice — thanks for the clear notes and the attached redlines. Quick summary of where Redwood stands and next steps below. Looping in Karthik (product) and Marissa (legal) for the technical and contract points.

Short answers up front:
- "Data closure": Redwood will perform logical erasure (data made inaccessible and removed from active indexes) within the agreed erasure window. For cold backups/snapshots we do not proactively shred physical blocks immediately; instead we implement a verified tombstone + retention clock and then remove blobs/pages on the next scheduled media reclamation cycle. We can provide a deletion manifest and an audit-log entry showing the manifest creation.
- Carve-out for named log streams: we can support per-stream retention exceptions requested by customers, but they need to be scoped in the SOW/Annex and will incur a small incremental storage charge and an SLA to deliver export/evidence on request.

Open items for redline resolution:
1) How long after customer-initiated erasure we should expect physical reclaim on cold snapshots (we propose 'within the next scheduled media maintenance cycle, typically within 90 days' — see suggested language in the attached).
2) Evidence format: Marissa and I prefer a combination of (a) deletion manifest, (b) audit log entry ID, and (c) optionally a cert-of-removal when the physical reclaim completes. HelioMetrics asked for a certificate — we can provide it, but it will be generated once reclaim completes (so timing differs from logical erasure).

Propose a short alignment call tomorrow at 10am PT to walk the redlines and agree annex language. If that works, please confirm and we'll send calendar invite.

- Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Account Exec, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Hi Alice, Dylan —

From legal's side, a few concrete edits that would close this loop quickly:

1) Replace Helmets-style wording "destruction" with "physical media reclamation" when discussing backups to avoid implying an immutable one-time shred; add an acceptance criteria clause for the certificate of removal (what metadata must be present: timestamp, manifest id, operator id).

2) For the per-stream carve-out, we need the request to be made in writing to support auditability and to include: stream identifier, retention period requested, legal/regulatory justification, and billing contact. We'll add a short template Annex to the DPA for that.

3) Evidence delivery timing: logical erasure evidence (manifest + audit log entry) should be provided within 7 business days of request. Certificate-of-removal will be provided after physical reclaim completes — we expect typical reclaim windows to be 30-120 days depending on storage tier. We will not warrant an exact day for physical media deletion in the DPA but we can commit to the reclaim window and provide periodic progress updates in the Ops Console.

Karthik — can you prepare suggested language for the Annex and the ops-exception template? Dylan — if Helio agrees, Marissa is ready to accept the certificate wording below (included as text in the second attached).
